title: Social Perceptions of English Spelling Variation on Twitter: A Comparative Analysis of Human and LLM Responses
abstract: arXiv:2511.23041v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Spelling variation (e.g. funnnn vs. fun) can influence the social perception of texts and their writers: we often have various associations with different forms of writing (is the text informal? does the writer seem young?). In this study, we focus on the social perception of spelling variation in online writing in English and study to what extent this perception is aligned between humans and large language models (LLMs). Building on sociolinguistic methodology, we compare LLM and human ratings on three key social attributes of spelling variation (formality, carefulness, age). We find generally strong correlations in the ratings between humans and LLMs. However, notable differences emerge when we analyze the distribution of ratings and when comparing between different types of spelling variation.

translated_title: Twitter上英语拼写变体的社会感知：人类与大语言模型回应的比较分析
translated_abstract: 拼写变体（例如 funnnn 与 fun）会影响人们对文本及其作者的社会感知：我们常常对不同的书写形式抱有各种联想（文本是否非正式？作者看起来是否年轻？）。本研究聚焦于英语在线写作中拼写变体的社会感知，探讨这种感知在人类与大语言模型（LLM）之间的一致程度。基于社会语言学方法论，我们比较了LLM与人类对拼写变体三个关键社会属性（正式度、谨慎度、年龄）的评分。我们发现人类与LLM的评分之间总体上存在较强的相关性。然而，在分析评分分布以及比较不同类型的拼写变体时，出现了显著的差异。
tldr: 本研究基于社会语言学方法比较人类与大语言模型对英语拼写变体社会属性的评分，发现两者总体高度相关，但在评分分布和不同拼写变体类型上存在显著差异。
en_tdlr: This study compares human and LLM ratings of the social perceptions of English spelling variation using sociolinguistic methodology, finding generally strong correlations but notable differences in rating distributions and across different types of spelling variation.
